quote: const total = lines.reduce((sum, l) => sum + l.qty * l.price, 0);
title: Total is summed from unrounded float prices, so it disagrees with the displayed unit prices and drifts from cents
evidence: Driven: price 1.005 with quantity 1000. The row shows `1000 × 1.00` (toFixed(2) on the price, line 8) while the total uses 1.005 and shows 1005.00. The payload sends 1.005. Money is held as binary floats, and the same arithmetic sits in the render function (domain leak).
failing_case: Add a line with quantity 1000 and price 1.005. The row reads 1000 × 1.00, which a reader would add up to 1000.00, but the total reads 1005.00. The invoice is overstated by 5.00 against what the screen displays.
remediation: Store prices as integer minor units, rounded once at input, and compute the total in one pure, tested function (for example `invoiceTotal(lines)`). The view only displays its result.

title: Price check accepts Infinity and 1e400, so the total shows Infinity and the payload carries null
evidence: Driven in Chromium: price "Infinity" passes `price > 0`. The list shows `2 × Infinity`, #total shows `Infinity`, and the POST body to /api/invoices contains `"price":null` (JSON.stringify turns Infinity into null). `1e400` parses to Infinity the same way. validQuantity also accepts any digit string, so 99999999999999999999 is kept as an imprecise float.
failing_case: Type price `1e400` (or `Infinity`), quantity 2, Add line, then Send invoice. The screen shows a total of Infinity and the server receives price null for that line.
remediation: Add one price normaliser at the boundary: require a finite number, match /^\d+(\.\d{1,2})?$/, set an upper bound, and bound the quantity as well. Reject anything else with a visible message.

title: A successful send shows nothing and leaves the lines in place, and the counter is never displayed
evidence: Traced and driven: after a 200 response the page is unchanged. `sentCount` is never read anywhere. `lines` is not cleared, so the next Send posts the same lines again (two POSTs carried the same body).
failing_case: Click Send, get a 200. The user sees no confirmation, assumes it failed and clicks again 1+ s later. The same invoice is created twice.
remediation: On success, show an announced status ("Invoice sent"), clear or lock the sent lines, and remove or display the counter.

title: Void invoice is shown to a user who can never use it, and the click does nothing, with no explanation
evidence: The signed-in user is {roles: ["viewer","billing"]} (line 2) and canVoid requires "admin". Driven: clicking #void sent no request and showed no dialog or text. The button in index.html:24 is enabled and styled like Send.
failing_case: Sam clicks Void invoice. The handler returns on line 32, the page shows nothing, and Sam cannot tell whether the invoice was voided or the click was refused.
remediation: Do not render the control without permission, or render it disabled with a visible reason ("Only admins can void invoices"). If a click is refused, say so in an announced message.

title: Double-send guard is a one-second timer, not an in-flight lock, so a slow request can be sent twice
evidence: Traced: tooSoon() only compares timestamps. The Send button is never disabled while the fetch is pending (app.js:24-29). Driven: two clicks 1.1 s apart produced two POSTs of the same lines. The guard also stays consumed after a failed send, so a retry within 1 s is silently ignored with no message (app.js:25).
failing_case: On a connection where /api/invoices takes more than 1 s, click Send, wait 1.1 s, click again. Two identical invoices are created.
remediation: Disable the button and set an in-flight flag in a try/finally around the request, and send an idempotency key with the request. Drop the timestamp guard.

title: A whitespace-only client passes `required`, is trimmed to empty, and is added as a line with no client
evidence: Driven: client " " satisfied the native required check. The row rendered as `: 1000 × 1.00` and the payload sent `"client":""`. Nothing re-checks the value after the trim.
failing_case: Type three spaces as the client, a valid quantity and price, then Add line. An invoice line with no client name is added and later sent.
remediation: Check the trimmed value after trimming and reject an empty one with a field error, or add a pattern attribute that rejects whitespace-only input.

title: Invalid quantity or price is dropped silently: no message, no focus, no marker on the field
evidence: Driven: quantity 0 and quantity abc each returned with no list change, no text and no error. The fields keep their values. The quantity and price inputs have no `required` or error markup (index.html:16, 18).
failing_case: Type quantity 2.5 and click Add line. Nothing happens. The user does not learn that only whole numbers are accepted.
remediation: Show a per-field error next to the input ("Quantity must be a whole number of 1 or more"), link it with aria-describedby and aria-invalid, and move focus to the first invalid field.

title: Send posts an empty invoice when there are no lines
evidence: Driven: on a fresh page, clicking Send issued POST /api/invoices with body `[]`. Nothing in the handler checks `lines.length`.
failing_case: Open the page and click Send invoice. An empty invoice is submitted.
remediation: Return early with a message ("Add at least one line") when there are no lines, and keep the button disabled until one exists.

quote: const res = await fetch("/api/invoices", { method: "POST", body: JSON.stringify(lines) });
title: Send and Void have no catch, so a network failure is an unhandled rejection with no message
evidence: Driven: with the route aborted, clicking Send raised a page error `Failed to fetch`. No dialog and no on-page text appeared. The `!res.ok` branch only covers HTTP errors, not a rejected fetch. The Void handler (line 33) has the same gap.
failing_case: Go offline, then click Send invoice. Nothing visible happens. The user cannot tell whether the invoice went out and may retry, or assume it was sent.
remediation: Wrap both requests in try/catch. Show an inline, announced error that names the cause and the next step ("No connection. The invoice was not sent. Check your network and try again."). Keep the draft.

title: Void is a one-click irreversible action that names no invoice, has no confirm, and reports no success
evidence: app.js:33 sends no body and no id, so the server cannot know which invoice to void. app.js:34 only reports failure, and there is no confirm step before the call. The client never holds an invoice id (app.js:20,26 post bare lines).
failing_case: An admin clicks Void by accident. The request is sent immediately. It voids whatever the server guesses (last, or all). There is no success text, so the admin cannot tell what happened.
remediation: Send the invoice id in the body. Put a confirm dialog ('Void invoice INV-123? This cannot be undone') in front of the call. Show a status message on success and name the voided invoice.

title: The only void permission check in the payload runs in the browser, from a client-held role list
evidence: app.js:2 builds `user` in client code. app.js:33 posts to /api/invoices/void with no credential or user in the request. No server code is in the payload, so no server-side check can be shown. The rubric row 'the client trusted to enforce limits' applies. Server code is not in the payload, so this is inferred.
failing_case: Any viewer opens the console and runs fetch('/api/invoices/void',{method:'POST'}), or sets user.roles.push('admin'). If the endpoint relies on this guard, the invoice is voided.
remediation: Enforce the admin role on the server for /api/invoices/void from the session, and treat the client check as a UI hint only. Add a test that a non-admin session gets 403.

title: Each client name is a link to #, which does nothing and adds a tab stop per line
evidence: Traced and driven: the rendered anchor has href="#", so activating it scrolls to the top and adds `#` to the URL. The title duplicates the link text. XSS is escaped correctly here: the hostile client string rendered inert.
failing_case: A keyboard user tabs through every client name, presses Enter, and the page jumps to the top with no result.
remediation: Render the client name as plain text (a span), or link it to a real client page.

title: After Add line the form keeps its values and focus stays on the button, so a second click adds a duplicate line
evidence: Driven: after a valid add the input values were unchanged (the `x` client remained after the later attempts). Nothing in the submit handler resets the form or moves focus.
failing_case: Enter a line, click Add line twice, and two identical lines are added. The total doubles.
remediation: Call e.target.reset() and focus #client after a successful add.

title: The live region is rebuilt wholesale, so every add re-announces the whole list, and the total is not announced
evidence: app.js:7 sets list.innerHTML for every render. Screen readers treat the replaced children as new content. The total in the <output> at index.html:22 is updated by textContent outside the live list. Traced.
failing_case: With ten lines, adding the eleventh makes a screen reader read all eleven again, and then it never speaks the new total.
remediation: Append only the new <li>, and announce 'Line added; total 12.50' in a separate role=status element.
